findings.title: Team admin/owner check requires both admin and owner roles
findings.body: The code computes `isTeamAdminOrOwner` as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. That makes the action available only to users who are both a team admin and a team owner, which is normally impossible. A user who is only an admin or only an owner is denied, despite the variable name and the UI exposing the action to `booking.isUserTeamAdminOrOwner`. This should use `||`.

findings.title: Guest email comparisons are case-sensitive, bypassing blacklist and duplicate checks
findings.body: `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is split and lowercased, but each `guest` is compared as supplied. A guest address such as `User@Example.com` will bypass `user@example.com`. In addition, the comparison against existing `booking.attendees` is case-sensitive, so the same email with different case can be added more than once. Normalize guest emails before filtering and deduplicating.

findings.title: Unbounded and duplicate guest list accepted at API
findings.body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` accepts `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()` and no uniqueness constraint. A direct tRPC caller can submit an arbitrarily large list, causing a large `createMany`, many external calendar API updates, and many invitation emails in one request. Add a sane maximum and reject duplicate entries at the schema or handler level.

findings.title: No status or end-time check: guests can be added to past bookings
findings.body: The handler only checks that the booking exists and that the caller has some role; it never rejects past bookings or disallowed statuses. The UI also includes the add-guests action under edit for past confirmed bookings (`apps/web/components/booking/BookingListItem.tsx` line 554). This allows new invitations and external calendar updates for events that have already ended. Reject bookings whose end time has passed and disallowed statuses.

findings.title: Database commit before external calendar update leaves unretryable partial state
findings.body: The new attendees are written to Postgres at line 92 before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` on line 165. That external call is not covered by a try/catch or transaction, so if it fails the request errors while the new attendees remain. Retrying then sees them as already existing (`uniqueGuests.length === 0`) and returns `BAD_REQUEST`, so the booking can be left permanently out of sync unless rows are manually removed. Add compensation handling or perform/validate the calendar update before committing, and make retries idempotent.

findings.title: External calendar update uses caller credentials instead of booking organizer credentials
findings.body: `EventManager` is constructed with `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. Since attendees and team admins/owners are allowed to call this handler, the credentials belong to the caller, not the owner of the booking/destination calendar. For such callers the calendar event is likely not updated or an update is attempted against the wrong account. The handler even fetches `booking.user.credentials` but never uses them. Use the booking organizer's credentials for `EventManager`.

findings.title: New add-guests emails ignore event-type email suppression settings
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not receive or check `eventTypeMetadata` and always sends organizer, team-member, and attendee emails. Other comparable functions (`sendLocationChangeEmails`, `sendScheduledEmails`) honor `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`. As a result, event types configured to disable host or attendee emails will still emit these notifications when guests are added.
